rfi.title: French right backs Macron's plan to put public spending limits in Constitution
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron is reportedly considering a constitutional reform to curb public deficits, with right-wing parties and the far-right National Rally signalling their willingness to support the move. The proposal could bring MPs and senators together for a vote as early as January, just months before the 2027 presidential election.

rfi.title: Cop31 climate talks collapse as EU rejects deal that omits fossil fuels
rfi.description: The Cop31 climate summit in Turkey has ended in disarray after the European Union and several other countries rejected a proposed global agreement that failed to explicitly mention fossil fuels. The breakdown, after more than two weeks of negotiations and a record 44 hours of overtime, marks a major setback for international climate diplomacy, with deep divisions over energy policy and financial support for developing nations left unresolved.

rfi.title: EU proposes digital tax to fund budget as France and Germany clash over cuts
rfi.description: The European Union has unveiled plans to tax the world's biggest digital companies to help finance its next long-term budget, as Brussels seeks to overcome deep divisions between member states over spending priorities. The proposal has already drawn criticism from France and Germany, highlighting the challenge of securing an agreement before the end of the year.

rfi.title: Who gets Europe's scrap? Industry fights over future of waste exports
rfi.description: A fight over scrap metal is pitting recyclers against manufacturers, with India and Egypt lobbying to keep buying tonnes of it from Europe to be melted down and reused.

rfi.title: Nepal's first climate loss and damage payout falls far short of needs
rfi.description: Nepal is set to become the first country to receive money from the UN's Loss and Damage Fund following devastating floods in August. But the provisional €19 million allocation covers less than 1 percent of the damage – and survivors are still waiting for help.

rfi.title: Students and unions unite for sixth weekend of protests across France
rfi.description: Thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Saturday for a sixth consecutive weekend of protests against rising living costs, deteriorating public services and growing inequality. The movement, which began with student demonstrations in September, has since broadened into a nationwide campaign and inspired similar rallies elsewhere in Europe.

rfi.title: 'I captured those defining moments when American youth were waking up'
rfi.description: French photographer Jean-Pierre Laffont has been making his mark on the history of photojournalism for six decades. Based in the US since 1964, Laffont has documented a country in profound transformation, covering the civil rights movement, anti-Vietnam War protests, the rise of the women’s and gay rights movements and life at the White House.

rfi.title: Traditional French tapestry captures fantastical world of Japanese anime
rfi.description: The French town of Aubusson is renowned for producing some of the world's finest tapestries. Now its weavers are using centuries-old techniques to reimagine scenes from the fantastical films of Japanese animators Studio Ghibli – and unearthing some unexpected connections in the process.

rfi.title: National Assembly backs greater legal protection for police using firearms
rfi.description: France's parliament has approved legislation giving police officers greater legal protection when using their firearms, prompting fierce criticism from rights groups who warn it could make it harder to investigate alleged police brutality. The government insists the measure is needed to protect officers carrying out increasingly demanding duties.

rfi.title: French court finds racism played role in police beating of black music producer
rfi.description: A French court has handed down prison sentences to three police officers for the violent assault of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020, ruling that racism was an aggravating factor in a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police brutality and racial discrimination.

rfi.title: Former PM de Villepin launches 2027 presidential bid with warning to far right
rfi.description: Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin has announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election, promising to restore France's international influence, tackle growing inequality and challenge the rise of the far right. The veteran conservative also delivered a blistering assessment of President Emmanuel Macron's leadership, accusing him of allowing the country's political and social divisions to deepen.

rfi.title: France must change or 'risk losing' overseas territories, former PM tells RFI
rfi.description: France's territories outside Europe are a major strategic asset, giving it a foothold on five continents and in three oceans. Yet Paris has long been accused of neglecting the nearly 3 million people living outside mainland France, who face deep economic and social inequalities. With calls for independence growing, former prime minister Manuel Valls warns that France risks losing its overseas territories unless it radically changes its relationship with them.

rfi.title: Cost of living protests set to continue across Europe over weekend
rfi.description: Protests across Europe against conditions in schools, housing and the soaring cost of living are set to continue throughout the weekend, with hundreds of thousands expected to take to the streets in countries across the continent – including France, Belgium, Italy, Spain and the United Kingdom.

rfi.description: Deep divisions over fossil fuels and financial support for poorer nations pushed the Cop31 climate summit in Turkey beyond its scheduled closing day on Friday, as nearly 200 countries struggled to agree on how to tackle global warming.

lemonde.description: Le parcours démarrera lundi 23 novembre avec l’objectif de rejoindre la ville des Yvelines. Sollicités, certains marcheurs de 1983 sont circonspects sur l’impact d’une nouvelle édition.

lemonde.title: La Corse placée en vigilance orange pour des vents violents à partir de lundi ; l’Ain et le Jura touchés par de fortes pluies et face à des risques d’inondations
lemonde.description: Des pointes jusqu’à 170 km/h seront possibles dans la péninsule du Cap-Corse, lundi, alors que des cumuls de pluie exceptionnels sont attendus sur le Haut-Jura et les plateaux, dimanche. Dans le Pas-de-Calais, la vigilance orange est maintenue pour la Canche.

france24fr.title: Elections générales en RD Congo, la Symocel doute de la possibilité de tenir les délais
france24fr.description: En RD Congo, se dirige-t-on vers un report des élections générales ? Les scrutins sont prévus en décembre 2028. Dans un rapport publié en novembre, la Symocel, l’une des missions d’observation électorale, doute de la possibilité de tenir ce délai...

france24fr.title: Libye : deux navires attaqués par des drones maritimes, dont un bateau russe
france24fr.description: Un incendie s'est déclaré dimanche après une explosion à bord d'un navire russe dans la base navale de Benghazi, en Libye. Le ministère de la Santé des autorités de l'Est a indiqué que le bateau avait été "ciblé par des drones maritimes". Dans la soirée, un deuxième bateau, dont le pavillon n'a pas été communiqué, a été attaqué dans le même port.

france24fr.title: Philippe Sands : "l'arrêt de la CIJ fait partie des moments-clés qui changent l'Histoire"
france24fr.description: La Cour Internationale de Justice a reconnu un génocide commis par la Birmanie à l'encontre de la minorité musulmane des Rohingya. La CIJ demande à ce que les réfugiés rohingya, pour la plupart entassés dans des camps au Bangladesh, puissent revenir en Birmanie et être indemnisés. L'avocat franco-britannique Philippe Sands, l'un des avocats qui ont représenté la Gambie contre la Birmanie devant la CIJ, était l'Invité d'Au Cœur de l'Info.

france24fr.title: Caroline Toby : "sans vidéosurveillance, Michel Zecler aurait été victime d'une erreur judiciaire"
france24fr.description: Le producteur Michel Zecler avait été passé à tabac en 2020 par trois policiers dans l'entrée de son studio d'enregistrement à Paris. Les policiers avaient établi un faux procès-verbal l'accusant de violences; or les images de vidéosurveillance avaient invalidé leur version. Les policiers viennent d'être condamnés à de la prison ferme, avec interdiction d'exercer leur métier. Le caractère raciste de ces violences a aussi été reconnu. Interview de Caroline Toby, avocate de Michel Zecler.

france24fr.title: Choose France : les entreprises françaises prêtent à investir 42,5 milliards d'euros
france24fr.description: Les entreprises tricolores projettent d'investir 42,5 milliards d'euros en France lors du sommet Choose France qui se déroulera lundi, a détaillé l'Élysée dimanche soir. Malgré une situation économique compliquée dans le pays, plus de 200 projets industriels français seront mis à l'honneur.

france24fr.title: La COP31 s'achève sur un échec, l'UE rejette la proposition d'accord final
france24fr.description: La COP31 ​se dirigeait dimanche 22 novembre vers un échec et le rejet par une majorité de pays du texte de conclusion présenté par la Turquie et l'Australie, qui pilotaient les négociations, un compromis ​jugé bien trop timoré par nombre de pays participants.

france24fr.title: Corée du Sud : démission du ministre de l'Éducation après un scandale de triche à l'IA
france24fr.description: Le ministre de l'Éducation sud-coréen a démissionné dimanche 22 novembre, emporté par un scandale de triche à l'intelligence artificielle qui a semé le doute quant à la bonne tenue des sacro-saints examens d'entrée à l'université.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : au moins deux morts après une frappe de drone russe contre un immeuble résidentiel
france24fr.description: Au ​moins deux personnes ont été tuées et une ​dizaine d'autres pourraient encore se trouver piégées sous les décombres d'un immeuble résidentiel frappé par un drone russe ​ce dimanche ‌22 novembre matin dans l'oblast de Kiev, ⁠ont déclaré le président Volodymyr Zelensky et des responsables locaux.

france24fr.title: De la Seine-Saint-Denis à la Nasa, retour sur le parcours d'Allan Petre
france24fr.description: L'ingénieur aérospatial Allan Petre a intégré la Nasa a 24 ans, ce qui fait de lui l'un des plus jeunes Français à y parvenir. Il publie "Astro Allan", une bande-dessinée retraçant son parcours.

france24fr.title: Climat : la COP31 échoue devant la division des pays sur les énergies fossiles
france24fr.description: La COP31, la plus longue conférence de l'ONU sur le climat de l'histoire, s'est terminée sur un échec ce dimanche 22 novembre à Antalya en Turquie, après le rejet par l'Union européenne et d'autres pays d'un projet de décision finale omettant les énergies fossiles.

france24fr.title: COP31 à Antalya : pas d'accord en vue ?
france24fr.description: La COP31 à Antalya est déjà la COP la plus longue de l’histoire, avec 44 heures de prolongations. Les négociations s’enlisent sur les énergies fossiles. Nous en parlons avec notre correspondante Jenna Le Bras.

france24fr.title: COP31 à Antalya : la plus longue COP de l'histoire s'achève sur un échec
france24fr.description: La COP31, la plus longue conférence de l'ONU sur le climat de l'histoire, s'est terminée sur un échec dimanche 22 novembre à Antalya, en Turquie, après le rejet par l'Union européenne et d'autres pays d'un projet de décision finale omettant les énergies fossiles. "On ressent de la déception et beaucoup de colère, parce que ce scénario aurait pu être évité", rapporte notre invitée Marine Pouget, responsable de la gouvernance internationale sur le climat au sein du Réseau Action Climat.

france24fr.title: Échec de la COP31 à Antalya : "Nous sommes passés à côté d'une opportunité"
france24fr.description: "Nous sommes passés à côté d'une opportunité", a reconnu le président de la COP après de très longues négociations. La COP31 à Antalya se termine donc sur un échec. Nous en parlons avec notre invitée Charlotte Chaussat, cofondatrice de la Coordination Climat. "Cette COP se passait dans un climat compliqué", rappelle-t-elle.

france24fr.title: COP31 : décryptage après son échec malgré 44 heures de prolongations
france24fr.description: La COP31 à Antalya se solde par un échec. Nous en parlons avec notre chroniqueuse Anne Corpet. "À la COP, les décisions se prennent par consensus : il faut l'unanimité. Le constat, c’est que l’alliance des pays hostiles à toute avancée a été plus forte que celle de ceux qui souhaitent avancer sur le plan climatique", explique-t-elle.

france24fr.title: France : un "marché de Noël d'autrefois" à Villeneuve d'Ascq
france24fr.description: La plupart des marchés de Noël ouvrent ce week-end en France, et certains ont choisi de maintenir les traditions et l’artisanat. Focus sur le marché de Noël "d’autrefois" de Villeneuve-d’Ascq.

france24fr.title: Israël : Eisenkot condamne des attaques de colons juifs en Cisjordanie
france24fr.description: Des ⁠colons israéliens ont attaqué ​dimanche 22 novembre des villages palestiniens de Cisjordanie occupée, provoquant des incendies et ​inscrivant des graffitis racistes, rapportent des témoins. Notre correspondant Stéphane Amar nous en dit plus.

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie occupée : Eisenkot condamne des attaques de colons et dénonce un "terrorisme juif"
france24fr.description: Une enquête a été ouverte dimanche par les autorités israéliennes après des incendies de véhicules palestiniens et des graffitis sur les murs dans quatre villages de Cisjordanie occupée. Gadi Eisenkot, chargé de former le prochain gouvernement israélien, a dénoncé un "terrorisme juif".

france24fr.title: Fuites au ministère de l'Intérieur : un mail jette des soupçons sur l'implication du préfet Moutouh
france24fr.description: La justice française soupçonne des fuites d'informations confidentielles du ministère de l'Intérieur vers le Rassemblement national. Un mail pourrait apporter des éléments sur le rôle de l'ancien secrétaire général de Beauvau et actuel préfet du Loiret et de la région Centre-Val de Loire, Hugues Moutouh, qui nie toute implication.

zeit.title: Unfall auf B26: 93-jähriger Fußgänger von Auto erfasst und schwer verletzt
Captagon, Cannabis, Betäubungsmittel: Syrische Behörden vernichten tonnenweise konfiszierte Drogen
zeit.description: 400 Millionen Tabletten des Aufputschmittels Captagon und Tonnen weiterer Rauschmittel sind in Syrien entsorgt worden. Die Machthaber bekämpfen die Drogenproduktion.

zeit.title: »Tatort« Frankfurt am Main: Ich dachte, ich sehe einen Geist
zeit.description: Mit einigem Fingerspitzengefühl macht dieser »Tatort« aus Frankfurt am Main einen Anschlag auf iranische Exilanten zu seinem Thema. Ein Glanzstück der Saison.

zeit.title: 0:1 beim MSV Duisburg: Nach Unterbrechung: Hansa verliert Topspiel in Unterzahl
Drohnenangriffe im Sudan: UN melden Angriff auf Wohngebiet in sudanesischer Hauptstadt
zeit.description: In der Provinz Khartum im Sudan sind Drohnenangriffe auf Wohnhäuser gemeldet worden. Drei Menschen wurden getötet, auch eine UN-Einrichtung sei beschädigt worden.

zeit.title: Antisemitismus: Israels Botschafter würdigt Mut von verletzter Aktivistin
Kalte Progression: Grüne werfen Söder »öffentliches Lamentieren« vor
zeit.description: CSU-Chef Markus Söder fordert »dringend einen Ausgleich der kalten Progression«. Die Opposition wirft ihm Inszenierung vor und warnt, er verspiele damit Vertrauen.

zeit.title: ATP Finals im Tennis: Keine Krönung: Zverev mit Final-Pleite gegen Alcaraz
ATP Finals: Alexander Zverev verpasst dritten Titel bei ATP Finals
zeit.description: Carlos Alcaraz besiegt Alexander Zverev im Endspiel der ATP Finals. Zverev macht zu viele Fehler, aus Frust wirft er seinen Schläger auf den Boden.

zeit.title: Stuttgarter Kammerorchester: Beethoven kann wirklich charmant sein
zeit.description: Nächstes Jahr feiert die Musikwelt den 200. Todestag des Klassikers aller Klassiker. Gibt’s da eigentlich noch etwas Neues zu entdecken? Ja, hier!

zeit.title: Fußball-Bundesliga: Hamburger Muheim im Nordderby an der Wade verletzt
AfD in NRW: »Scharmützel«, »Heckenschützen«, so sprechen sie hier übereinander
zeit.description: In Nordrhein-Westfalen beschloss die AfD, welche Themen sie im Landtagswahlkampf setzen will. Unschöne Debatten um den Begriff »Remigration« will man lieber vermeiden.

zeit.title: Versteckte Steuererhöhung: Söder lässt bei kalter Progression nicht locker
Versteckte Steuererhöhung: Söder lässt bei kalter Progression nicht locker
Bundeshaushalt: Wüst weist Söders Forderung zur kalten Progression zurück

observador.title: Trump pondera atacar Irão sem acordo até ao Ano Novo
observador.description: O Presidente norte-americano "está inclinado" a retomar os bombardeamentos no Irão, caso não se alcance um acordo diplomático até ao Ano Novo. As negociações permanecem estagnadas.

observador.title: Brasil. O futebolista que pôs Tolstoi nos tops das livrarias
observador.description: Gustavo Scarpa, que já foi considerado o melhor jogador do Brasil, faz sucesso como crítico literário nas redes sociais e gerou um fenómeno de leituras. Trineto de Tolstoi agradeceu-lhe publicamente.

observador.title: As notícias das 21h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: A "vingança" adiada por culpa própria: Benfica empata dérbi
observador.description: Pavilhão João Rocha recebeu um autêntico hino do hóquei em patins com 12 golos, dois hat-tricks de Rampulla e Pau Bargalló e um empate resgatado pelo Benfica nos últimos minutos com menos um (6-6).

observador.title: Chefe das secretas. Trump chamar amigo a Putin é "adequado"
observador.description: Jay Clayton defende que é "totalmente adequado" que o Presidente norte-americano, Donald Trump, se refira ao homólogo russo, Vladimir Putin, como seu amigo.

observador.title: Itália é o 12º país a aprovar o Tesla FSD e o 1º dos grandes
observador.description: O sistema de condução autónoma supervisionada da Tesla foi aprovado pela Itália, o 12.º país europeu (e o primeiro dos grandes) a permitir o uso desta tecnologia na via pública.

observador.title: COP31. A cimeira mais longa de sempre acabou sem nada
observador.description: Foram duas semanas de negociações, 44 horas de prolongamento e quatro versões do texto. Mesmo assim, a COP31 acabou sem acordo. Houve duas barricadas, a dos ambiciosos e a dos produtores de petróleo.

observador.title: Durmo 8 horas, acordo cansado. Porquê? Resposta aos ouvintes
observador.description: Depois do episódio do sono, recebemos tantas dúvidas que parámos tudo para responder. Insónia, turnos, filhos pequenos, melatonina... Gustavo Jesus responde às suas  perguntas. Episódio especial.

observador.title: Como o Governo quer chegar ao "gold standard" da imigração
observador.description: Houve três mil atendimentos diários e entupiu-se a Casa da Moeda para pôr processos em dia. Até março, Governo espera por dados revistos do INE. AIMA e confederações alertam para problemas.

observador.title: 20h. José Luís Carneiro nega "jogos políticos" para negociar
observador.description: O secretário-geral do PS esclarece: não houve quaisquer diálogos, negociações ou acordos com outros partidos para a viabilização de propostas de alteração ao Orçamento do Estado para 2027.

observador.title: 30 calendários do Advento para contar os dias até ao Natal
observador.description: Dos cafés e chocolates aos produtos de cosmética e perfumaria, passando por joalharia, livros e meias: uma seleção que faz o mês de dezembro passar a voar até a chegada do Pai Natal.

observador.title: O discurso de André Ventura nas entrelinhas
observador.description: André Ventura encerrou a VII Convenção do Chega aliviado pelos resultados eleitorais e certo de que tem a confiança e a força necessárias dentro do partido para chegar ao Governo.

observador.title: COP31. Nórdicos reafirmam importância do multilateralismo
observador.description: Dinamarca, Finlândia, Noruega, Suécia e Islândia reafirmaram a importância do multilateralismo no combate às alterações climáticas. COP31 terminou sem acordo político global.

observador.title: Prestianni recoloca encarnados na frente (1-2, 63')
observador.description: Benfica regressa à competição depois das seleções com estreia na Taça de Portugal frente ao campeão em título, Torreense, que volta ao Jamor depois do triunfo frente ao Sporting. Siga aqui em direto.

observador.title: Capitão do Boca Juniors desmaia em direto na flash interview
observador.description: Leandro Paredes falava a um jornalista durante uma entrevista rápida depois de o Boca Juniors ganhar a Taça Sul-Americana por 2-0 frente ao Atlético Mineiro. Jogador já confirmou que está bem.

observador.title: Dino d'Santiago vence mais um prémio nos EUA
observador.description: O músico Dino d'Santiago venceu o prémio de Melhor Artista de Afro Jazz nos Diaspora Creatives Awards, anunciou este domingo em Braga.

observador.title: Carlitos não é o melhor oficial – é o melhor em tudo o resto
observador.description: Zverev chegou à final como número 1, só com vitórias e sem ceder sets mas foi atropelado pela melhor versão de Carlos Alcaraz, que mesmo sem estar a 100% deu um autêntico show em Turim para a vitória.

observador.title: Para a história mas sem história: FC Porto goleia Sporting
observador.description: Dois golos nos dez minutos iniciais deram o mote, uma obra de arte de Mariana Negrão fez o resto: FC Porto goleou Sporting por claros 5-1 e subiu ao segundo lugar da Liga no primeiro clássico oficial.

nzz.title: Carlos Alcaraz gewinnt die ATP-Finals – und liefert Zverevs Kritikern neues Futter
nzz.description: Nach vier Monaten Verletzungspause krönt der spanische Tennisstar sein Comeback. Als erst vierter Mann nach Agassi, Federer und Djokovic hat er alle vier Majors und das Jahresendturnier gewonnen.

nzz.title: VIDEO - Wann Aufrüstung gefährlich wird: Europas Dilemma mit Russland
nzz.description: Russland produziert immer mehr Drohnen und Munition. Europas Nato-Staaten reagieren mit neuen Abwehrsystemen und weitreichenden Waffen. Doch was zur Abschreckung dienen soll, könnte im Ernstfall eine gefährliche Eskalation auslösen. Ein hypothetisches Szenario in Kaliningrad zeigt, wie schnell militärische Gegenschläge zum nuklearen Risiko werden können.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Die USA nach den Midterms: Demokraten im Repräsentantenhaus so stark wie zuletzt 1992
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus den USA während der zweiten Amtszeit von Präsident Donald Trump.

nzz.title: Der FC Zürich zeigt auch gegen St. Gallen, dass der Cheftrainer Marcel Koller mit der jungen Mannschaft auf gutem Weg ist
nzz.description: Beim attraktiven 2:2 gegen die Ostschweizer lässt sich der Kulturwandel im FCZ begutachten: Spieler bekommen Vertrauen und zahlen es mit erfrischenden Leistungen zurück.

nzz.title: Libysche Streitkräfte fangen vor Bengasi mehr als zwölf Drohnenboote ab
nzz.description: Vor der libyschen Küste ist am Sonntag ein Handelsschiff unter maltesischer Flagge ins Visier eines Drohnenboots geraten. Bereits in der Nacht war es auf einem russischen Kriegsschiff in Bengasi zu einer schweren Explosion gekommen.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN POLIZEI - Explosion und Brand in Mehrfamilienhaus in Menziken AG
nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Schweiz.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die globale Klimapolitik erleidet einen Realitätsschock
nzz.description: Die jüngste Klimakonferenz, COP31, ist an den weltweiten Interessenkonflikten in der Klimapolitik gescheitert. Trotzdem schreitet die Energiewende voran.

nzz.title: Wollen die Bayern Jamal Musiala loswerden? Um den erkrankten Spieler ist eine heftige Diskussion entbrannt
nzz.description: Die Führungsetage des FC Bayern drängt offenbar auf Gehaltsverzicht – und stellt öffentlich infrage, ob Musiala je wieder seine alte Form erreicht. Auf der Jahreshauptversammlung kommt das schlecht an.

nzz.title: Ein Anthropic-Mitarbeiter will das berühmteste Rätsel der Mathematik gelöst haben. Was nützt ein Beweis, den kein Mensch versteht?
nzz.description: Bernhard Riemanns Problem gilt seit 167 Jahren als Heiliger Gral der Zahlentheorie. Der nun mithilfe der KI Claude erbrachte Nachweis umfasst viele Millionen Zeilen Computercode.

nzz.title: Die EU und die Schweiz sagen Nein und verhindern ein neues Klimaabkommen. Dahinter steckt ein Streit um Kohle, Öl und Geld
nzz.description: Am Weltklimagipfel in der Türkei haben fast 200 Staaten zwei Wochen lang über neue Massnahmen verhandelt. Die Einigung scheitert. Dennoch macht die Energiewende in vielen Regionen der Welt konkrete Fortschritte.

nzz.title: Slalom in Gurgl: Tanguy Nef wird Dritter – erstmals steht der 30-Jährige auf dem Weltcup-Podest
nzz.description: Einzig die beiden Norweger Timon Haugan und Eirik Hystad Solberg waren schneller als der Schweizer Skirennfahrer. Lucas Pinheiro Braathen scheidet beim ersten Lauf aus.

nzz.title: Ein russischer Frachter brennt im Finnischen Meerbusen – er wurde vermutlich von ukrainischen Drohnen getroffen
nzz.description: Die Ukraine weitet ihre Angriffe offenbar auf die offene See aus und greift ein russisches Schiff vor Finnland an. Während die Rettungsoperation läuft, verletzt ein russischer Militärhelikopter den finnischen Luftraum.

nzz.title: «Ganz Zürich hasst die Polizei!»: Der Jugendstreik war laut und wütend – doch schwere Krawalle blieben aus
nzz.description: Bei den landesweiten Protesten am Freitag ist es vereinzelt zu Scharmützeln gekommen. In Zürich waren kaum Teenager auf der Strasse. Dafür kann die viel kritisierte Polizei einen Erfolg verbuchen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Laut Selenski werden mindestens 14 Menschen nach russischem Drohnenangriff auf Wohnhaus vermisst
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: VIDEO - Bundesrat Pfister: «Wird die Vorlage zum Kriegsmaterialgesetz abgelehnt, schaden wir uns selbst»
nzz.description: Bundesrat Martin Pfister diskutiert bei «NZZ Standpunkte» die internationale Kritik am Schweizer Kriegsmaterialgesetz.

nzz.title: VIDEO «NZZ STANDPUNKTE» - «Ich bin entschlossen, im VBS zu bleiben», sagt Bundesrat Martin Pfister – und erteilt damit Gerüchten eine Absage
nzz.description: Die Bedrohung durch kriegerische Konflikte nimmt zu, viele europäische Länder rüsten massiv auf. Auch die Schweiz müsse aufwachen, so der Vorsteher des VBS. Er selber stehe bereit für die weitere Arbeit im Verteidigungsdepartement.

spiegel.title: Krieg in Sudan: Uno-Gebäude bei Drohnenangriff beschädigt
spiegel.description: Bei einem Drohnenangriff in der sudanesischen Hauptstadt Khartum sind nah Angaben der Uno mehrere Gebäude in einem Wohngebiet schwer beschädigt worden, darunter eins der Vereinten Nationen.

spiegel.title: Markus Söder: Hendrik Wüst lehnt Forderung zur kalten Progression ab
spiegel.description: NRW-Ministerpräsident Wüst stellt sich gegen die Forderung von Markus Söder, die kalte Progression auszugleichen. Man habe sich auf die Senkung der Stromsteuer geeinigt, mehr gebe der Haushalt nicht her.

spiegel.title: Midterms in den USA: Demokraten erreichen im Repräsentantenhaus historisch starke Mehrheit
spiegel.description: In den USA baut sich die blaue Welle bei den Zwischenwahlen weiter auf: Die Demokraten haben nach einem knappen Sieg in North Carolina eine historische Marke erreicht. Und es sind noch Wahlkreise offen.

spiegel.title: Finnland: »Sparta II« nach Brand in russische Gewässer geschleppt
spiegel.description: »Die beste und sicherste Lösung für Finnland«: Der vor der finnischen Küste durch einen Drohnenangriff in Brand geratene Frachter ist laut Grenzschutz in russisches Territorium zurückgeführt worden.

spiegel.title: Libyen: Explosion auf russischem Schiff – ukrainischer Angriff vermutet
spiegel.description: In einem Hafen der ostlibyschen Stadt Bengasi hat es eine Explosion auf einem russischen Kriegsschiff gegeben. Die Behörden gehen von einem Drohnenangriff aus.

spiegel.title: ATP Finals: Alexander Zverev verpasst Krönung seines Traumjahres gegen Carlos Alcaraz
spiegel.description: Er gewann die Grand-Slam-Turniere in Paris und New York, wurde erstmals die Nummer eins der Tenniswelt. Der Prestigesieg gegen den Topstar Carlos Alcaraz gelang Alexander Zverev aber nicht.

spiegel.title: Premier League: Pochettino soll United retten, erlebt 0:4-Debakel in Liverpool
spiegel.description: Mauricio Pochettino gab seinen Job als US-Nationaltrainer auf, um Manchester United zu alten Erfolgen zurückzuführen. Beim Start zeigte sich: Das wird sehr schwer. An diesem Tag lag das auch an Florian Wirtz.

spiegel.title: FC Arsenal: Lisa Baum bricht im Spiel mit Atemnot zusammen
spiegel.description: Ihr Zustand soll stabil sein, doch die Bilder waren schockierend: Mit einer Atemmaske musste die deutsche Fußballerin Lisa Baum bei einem Ligaspiel ihres Vereins FC Arsenal vom Feld gebracht werden.

spiegel.title: »Im Verhör«: Korrupte Justiz (3): Wie man sich einen Staatsanwalt kauft - SPIEGEL TV
spiegel.description: Drogenboss »Kosta« kann sein Glück kaum glauben. Seine Bande konnte einen deutschen Staatsanwalt korrumpieren. Ab jetzt wissen die Kriminellen, wie sie der Überwachung der Staatsanwaltschaft Hannover entgehen können.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: »Der Ukraine steht der härteste Kriegswinter bevor« – Militärexperte Franz-Stefan Gady
spiegel.description: Kyjiws Soldaten werden an der Front taktisch immer besser und machen kleine Fortschritte. Doch der Militärexperte Franz-Stefan Gady warnt: Russlands Kraft ist trotz gigantischer Verluste noch lange nicht erschöpft.

spiegel.title: Umgang mit Trauer: Wenn der Friedhof zum Ort für Freundinnen und Feiern wird
spiegel.description: Warum meine engsten Freundinnen und ich uns regelmäßig auf dem Friedhof treffen. Und dort gemeinsam ganz glückselig sind.

spiegel.title: Billy Joel versteigert Motorradsammlung für zwei Millionen Dollar

Bugs can acquire these parasites when feeding on infected mammals, while mammals can also become infected through encounters with infected bugs.

phys-org.title: Single feathers may reveal whether eastern black rails stay in Texas or migrate north
phys-org.description: High-stepping like you're in a marching band while dragging a rope through a wetland at night can make you wonder about your life choices. Several plastic bottles, each filled with two or three noisy cat toys, are attached to the rope. It's pitch black, and all I can hear are the cat toys jingling, the mosquitoes buzzing in my ears and the wetland grasses bouncing in the wind.

phys-org.title: The avian champions of long-distance migration keep surprising scientists

phys-org.title: Repeated bending strengthens sugar-based hydrogel instead of wearing it down

phys-org.title: Dropping degree requirements linked to higher pay for workers without degrees

For instance, if a job requires applicants to have earned a bachelor's or master's degree in a relevant subject, people without them may be excluded from the selection process, even if they have gained relevant skills through experience or professional training.

phys-org.title: Babies in ancient Greek colony started solid food at 3 months but nursed for nearly 4 years, chemical signatures suggest

phys-org.title: An ancient failed rift is reawakening inside one of Africa's oldest landmasses
phys-org.description: In April 2017, a magnitude 6.5 earthquake shook southern Africa from an unlikely place: the middle of the Kalahari Craton in eastern Botswana. Cratons are the ancient cores of continents, and this one is built from blocks of crust up to 3.7 billion years old. Geologists have long considered such regions too cold, too thick and too rigid to tear apart.

phys-org.title: Fermi's 14-year all-sky map bridges astronomy's elusive 'MeV gap'
phys-org.description: Gamma rays, the most high-energy type of electromagnetic radiation in the universe, have always had a blind spot. We've always had trouble measuring them in the "megaelectronvolt" (MeV) energy range, which astronomers have taken to calling the "MeV gap." phys-org.title: From screens in class to smart glasses, Norway rethinks new technologies

phys-org.title: What makes rock deep beneath continents break away and sink?
phys-org.description: We usually picture mountain building as rock being pushed upward. But deep beneath some mountain belts and volcanic arcs, the opposite can happen: dense rock at the base of the crust can become unstable, break away and sink hundreds of kilometers into the mantle, dragging part of the rigid outer shell of the Earth (the lithosphere) with it. Seismic images suggest that this process, known as lithospheric dripping, has occurred beneath the central Andes and California's Sierra Nevada.

phys-org.title: Device that measures strawberry skin's strength will aid breeders

The prototype measures the strength of strawberry skin, a key breeding consideration for the Australian Strawberry Breeding Program at Queensland's Department of Primary Industries.

undark.title: Australia’s Social Media Ban Has Not Worked — For Now
undark.description: New data coming out of Australia suggests that bans alone may not be an effective enough deterrent to stop children from using social media. But the research faces limitations. What does that mean for other countries considering similar restrictions?

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation

But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

proj-syn.title: Journalism Can Be More Than AI Fodder
proj-syn.description: As AI fundamentally alters the information environment, news publishers risk becoming little more than content suppliers for Big Tech. To avoid that fate, many are drawing on their archives and expertise to develop AI tools that allow them to operate and compete on their own terms.

proj-syn.title: Governing African Economies as They Are
proj-syn.description: Africa cannot overcome its development challenges by applying the same knowledge, economic, and innovation systems that helped create them. Imagining and governing new ways forward will require three intellectual ruptures.

proj-syn.title: Making Earth Cool Again
proj-syn.description: Climate multilateralism is evolving into a two-tiered system in which high-level negotiations toward shared commitments and the real-world implementation of climate solutions become more mutually supportive. Only by unleashing such virtuous cycles can we keep the 1.5ºC target for global warming within reach.

proj-syn.title: America’s Lame-Duck Autocrat
proj-syn.description: When autocrats suffer a defeat, they tend to double down, such as by intensifying repression at home or behaving more recklessly abroad. With two years left in office after historic midterm election losses, this is the road US President Donald Trump appears to be taking.

proj-syn.title: Getting Ukraine’s House in Order
proj-syn.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly opposed the idea of forming a national unity government. But bringing opposition leaders into the cabinet would ensure the checks on corruption and wayward bureaucratic action that Zelensky’s team can no longer provide.

proj-syn.title: What Adam Smith Missed
proj-syn.description: For all that he got right, the "founding father" of economics failed to see how technological innovations lead to market monopolization. If AI is left to the invisible hand, it will almost certainly increase economic and political inequality, causing even deeper social polarization and further undermining democracy.

proj-syn.title: China Ratchets Up Its Weaponization of Trade
proj-syn.description: Just as the US has been leveraging its large market and technological leadership for geopolitical ends, China is now using its dominance in critical minerals, industrial inputs, and specialized manufacturing machinery to coerce and punish other countries. The consequences, both economic and geopolitical, are far-reaching.

proj-syn.title: There Is Only One Thing to Talk About With Russia
proj-syn.description: The European security order’s foundational principle is never to tolerate aggression. There is no need to revise that order, as the Kremlin has proposed, only to wait for a Russian regime that is willing to respect other countries’ territorial integrity and uphold its own previous commitments.

proj-syn.title: The Truth About Global AI Governance
proj-syn.description: Because the current approach to global AI governance presumes that developing countries are full of eager adopters of AI who need to be cautioned about the technology's risks, it overlooks what their information environments and media markets actually need. A survey of researchers who study 71 countries sets the record straight.

proj-syn.title: Demography is the Achilles’ Heel of Dictatorships
proj-syn.description: Governments that manipulate population figures often end up deceiving themselves as much as the public. When autocratic leaders mistake inflated numbers for real national strength, they make costly strategic mistakes and fail to address their countries’ demographic decline until it is too late.

proj-syn.title: The Silver Lining of a Data-Center Slowdown
proj-syn.description: With leading AI labs under intense competitive pressure to keep advancing the frontier of the technology's capabilities, resistance to the build-out of computing resources is not such a bad thing. The more time we can buy, the greater our chances of maximizing the potential benefits and mitigating the risks.

proj-syn.title: What Nvidia’s Crisis Reveals About the Chip War
proj-syn.description: Export restrictions, like those depriving China of Nvidia’s most advanced chips, may buy time by curtailing a competitor's access to frontier capabilities made elsewhere. But in any technological conflict, policymakers must remember that slowing a rival is not the same as strengthening oneself.

proj-syn.title: When Export Restraints Are the Lesser Evil
proj-syn.description: Governments face pressure to protect domestic industries while preserving access to cheaper foreign goods. The recent EU-China car-export deal offers an uneasy compromise that protects European automakers while keeping Chinese cars available to consumers, making it preferable to prohibitive tariffs.

proj-syn.title: The Trade Losses That Nobody Counts
proj-syn.description: While much of the United Kingdom’s post-Brexit debate has focused on the monetary value of lost trade with the European Union, the composition of UK-EU trade flows warrants closer attention. A sharp decline in the variety of products shipped to Europe suggests that the economic costs have been greater than many realize.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Big Bet on Health Care
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s dependence on imported medicines and medical equipment leaves families exposed to exchange-rate fluctuations and hospitals at the mercy of global supply chains. Expanding domestic manufacturing is essential to reducing the cost of treatment and ensuring that more Nigerians can access quality care.

proj-syn.title: What Should the Nvidia Board Do?
proj-syn.description: The proper role of any corporate board is to strike a careful balance between stakeholders. In Nvidia's case, the board will have to consider not just the current trading price, but also how its decisions will affect the landscape in which it operates, its employees, and its license to trade.

proj-syn.title: The Roots of Macron’s Failure
proj-syn.description: Although French President Emmanuel Macron has certainly made mistakes, his troubled presidency is symptomatic of a deeper problem. In the end, he failed to build something truly enduring because he was seduced by the same monarchical impulse that is a recurring feature of French political culture.

proj-syn.title: Yalta in Shenzhen?
proj-syn.description: In principle, the planned summit of the US, Russian, and Chinese presidents could usefully address what should be done to limit the proliferation of nuclear weapons, ensure that AI is more a force for good than harm, and end ongoing wars and prevent new ones. But principle is one thing; in practice, we are likely to see something else.

crunchbase.description: What if solar farms could keep generating electricity after sunset with a little help from mirrors orbiting Earth? Or researchers could send an experiment into space for less than the price of a car? Our latest roundup also includes a company bringing AI to the old-school business of garbage hauling, another rethinking how factories are programmed, and a consumer brand betting that better breathing could become a big business.

crunchbase.title: What The Telecom Bust Taught Me About AI’s Debt Boom
crunchbase.description: The AI buildout’s growing reliance on debt echoes the telecom bubble, raising the risk that infrastructure spending will outpace the revenue needed to meet fixed repayment obligations. According to guest author David Spreng of Runway Growth Capital, even if AI fulfills its technological promise, borrowers’ survival will depend on realistic demand forecasts and debt tied to dependable cash flows, with missed timelines potentially forcing restructurings and bankruptcies.

crunchbase.title: The Blue Economy: The World’s Quietest Economic Engine And Its Smartest Cities
crunchbase.description: The $2.6 trillion blue economy is creating startup opportunities in maritime automation, clean energy and logistics, with blue tech funding nearing $10 billion through Q3 2026, driven largely by major defense deals. Alberto Onetti, chairman of Mind the Bridge, writes that ports are emerging as hubs for testing and scaling these technologies, but realizing their potential requires coordination among port authorities, startups, investors and policymakers.

crunchbase.title: What’s Next For Recruiting, Job Hunting And HR? More AI, Of Course
crunchbase.description: So far this year, venture backers have poured close to $4 billion into an assortment of global companies focused on recruiting, finding jobs and streamlining processes associated with HR and payroll management, Crunchbase data shows. Not surprisingly, the vast majority are also incorporating a heavy dose of AI.

crunchbase.title: Public Markets Are Frequently Wrong. The SaaSpocalypse Shows Us Why
crunchbase.description: The “SaaSpocalypse” selloff and uneven recovery exposed public markets’ difficulty distinguishing software companies that benefit from AI from those it threatens, particularly as deeply embedded platforms retain competitive advantages. In this guest essay, Richard Anton, co-founder and general partner of Oxx, argues that this volatility distorts private transaction pricing, undermines confidence in public ownership and makes IPOs less appealing to founders.

crunchbase.title: Anthropic Closes Up 17% After Massive IPO
crunchbase.description: The offering promises to be the public market event of the season, with the Claude creator seeing investor demand for shares well in excess of its capital-raising goals.

crunchbase.title: The Key Numbers I’m Watching As Anthropic Makes Its IPO Debut
crunchbase.description: Just three years after launching with zero revenue, Anthropic brought in $17 billion and says more than 11,900 customers now spend at least $100,000 a year. But its IPO filing also reveals enormous computing commitments and big questions about balancing growth with risks.

crunchbase.title: What To Measure When ARR Isn’t Enough
crunchbase.description: AI companies’ hybrid subscription, usage and outcome-based pricing makes headline ARR figures an unreliable measure of predictable revenue, often obscuring differences in customer commitments and spending patterns. Guest author Kenza Zayani, an early-stage investor at RTP Global, warns that as these businesses seek growth capital, investors increasingly expect evidence of retention, expansion, revenue predictability and sustainable margins to assess the durability of growth.

crunchbase.title: Sector Snapshot: Investors Turn Up The Volume On Voice AI
crunchbase.description: Voice AI is drawing billions of dollars from investors as startups find more ways to put it to work. According to Crunchbase data, companies developing or offering the technology have raised at least $9.5 billion in venture funding so far in 2026.
